answer: Each identity locks a 70-credit copper bond. Each delivery has a velvet seal bound to the seller key and a plume ticket for the buyer. If work is defective, the buyer files the plume ticket promptly; an auditor checks the record and, on confirmation, burns 35 and pays 35 to the buyer. The k-th defective delivery by one identity doubles the burn: first 35, second 70, third 140. For 1,000 fakes, bonds lock 70,000 and claims burn 35,000. An honest seller with no confirmed claim keeps the 70. A rented seal fails: the velvet seal is key-bound, so a mismatch voids the sale and burns the bond.
